overall_structure.value: Two-phase structure of γ-austenite matrix with irregularly shaped δ-ferrite. X-ray diffraction shows the constituent phases after cold rolling with 20% reduction are still γ-austenite and δ-ferrite together with an ordered DO3 phase, completely consistent with the as-cast steel strips; the δ-ferrite morphology and volume fraction do not change significantly after cold rolling. Nano-scale κ-carbides precipitate in the γ-austenite and ordered DO3 phases in the δ-ferrite.

source.reason: Slip band spacing measurements for the CR20% 3Cr strip (100 ± 15 nm) and the dislocation-blocking role of high-density slip bands are given in b0066, b0073; κ-carbide/dislocation interaction in b0082–b0083; δ-ferrite stability after cold rolling in b0062.

qualitative_or_quantitative_description.value: In the CR20% Cr-containing (3Cr) steel strips a higher density of slip bands than in the Cr-free strip is present; the high-density slip bands significantly block the movement of dislocations and increase the deformation difficulty, leading to an increase in strength. The smaller the slip band spacing, the greater the stress required for deformation (E. Welsch et al.).

Nano-scale κ-carbides act as reinforcing phases hindering dislocation glide by providing energy barriers; the decrease of κ-carbides caused by Cr addition contributes to the formation of dislocations and increases the density of the slip bands. At early strain, dislocations pile up and shear the κ-carbides leading to glide plane softening.

slip_behavior.value: Planar slip ({111} planar slip bands) present in the austenite of the CR20% steel strips. Measured average slip band spacing: 0Cr = 371 ± 47 nm, 3Cr = 100 ± 15 nm, 6Cr = 45 ± 13 nm; measured at least three different regions per specimen. The difference in slip band spacing is responsible for the difference in reinforcement effect after cold rolling — the smaller the slip band spacing, the stronger the reinforcement effect.

interface_notes.value: No significant change in the morphology and volume fraction of δ-ferrite after cold rolling; further annealing at 600 °C has no significant effect on the microstructure of the cold-rolled strips.

unmapped_findings: Measured chemical composition of the 3Cr steel strip (wt.%, Table 1): Mn 20.04, Al 9.09, C 1.23, Cr 3.09, S 0.0009, Fe Bal. (nominal Fe-20Mn-9Al-1.2C-3Cr).
Measured average density of the 3Cr steel strips is 6.69 g/cm3 (AccuPyc II 1340), between 0Cr (6.71 g/cm3) and 6Cr (6.66 g/cm3).

δ-ferrite volume fraction of the CR20% (cold-rolled) 3Cr strip is 12% (0Cr = 5%, 6Cr = 18%); cold rolling produces no significant change in the morphology and volume fraction of δ-ferrite relative to the as-cast state.
Average {111} planar slip band spacing in the CR20% 3Cr strip = 100 ± 15 nm (0Cr = 371 ± 47 nm; 6Cr = 45 ± 13 nm); smaller spacing gives stronger reinforcement after cold rolling.

After 20% cold rolling the yield strength and ultimate tensile strength of the Cr-containing strips are significantly higher than the Cr-free strip, in contrast to the as-cast condition where Cr addition decreased yield strength; higher density of slip bands in the Cr-containing cold-rolled strips blocks dislocation movement.

In the as-cast 3Cr alloy, ordered DO3 nanoparticles of size 30 ± 3 nm are densely distributed in the δ-ferrite, and the measured lattice parameters of the κ-carbides and γ-austenite are 0.387 nm and 0.376 nm respectively (as-cast condition, not the CR20% condition of this sample).
The addition of Cr increases the strain hardening rate of the CR20% steel strips; the strain hardening rate decreases gradually with increasing strain for the CR20% strips.

A double (slip-band and microband) hardening mechanism is proposed: hardening of slip bands acts at the early strain stage and hardening of microbands at the final strain stage; the number of nano-scale κ-carbides plays a crucial role in the strain hardening rate at the early strain stage.

The double-peak between 43.5° and 45.0° in XRD (attributed to (110)δ and (220)DO3) changes into a single peak upon annealing at 600 °C for 3 h, both for the as-cast and for the CR20% + annealed strips (annealing condition, not the CR20% condition of this sample).
